prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the driving range receding from the camera wearer's bright foreground limbs and held club (0.3–1.0 m away, within arm's reach) across the hitting mat, front ball tray, and grey barrier (1.5–2.0 m ahead) to the yellow bay-divider pipes (2.5–4.0 m ahead) and darkened turf beyond (over 6 m away). In Frame 1, the downward view places the wearer's extended left leg, right leg, and left arm in the near foreground above the flat mat surface, while across Frames 2 to 5 the wearer steps back and tilts their head up and down as both arms hold and raise the club vertically in front of the torso, partially occluding the mat, ball tray, and yellow divider behind it. In Frames 3 and 5, when the camera tilts high enough to include the upper field, the second golfer standing on the next mat 6–8 m ahead (Facing left toward the range and never looking toward the camera wearer, with a golf bag stand 2–3 m to their right at 8–10 m distance) appears as a faint dark silhouette against the black background, whereas this golfer is mostly cropped out at the top of Frame 2 and completely out of view in Frame 4. Compared to RGB, the depth map makes the smooth distance gradient of the turf and the 3D separation between the raised club shaft (0.4–0.8 m) and the background mat and dividers (1.5–4.0 m) immediately clear without confusion from the harsh overhead floodlight shadows cast on the grass. However, the depth map is unreliable on thin and small structures—the thin club shaft and head vanish in Frames 1, 4, and 5, the golf ball on the tee and spare clubs on the grass to the right (1.5–2.0 m) are largely lost, and Frame 5 suffers from a bright exposure washout across the entire bottom edge.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background entities on a black canvas, separating the camera wearer's close-up limbs (0.3–1.0 m away at the bottom of the frame) from the distant golfer on the forward mat (6–8 m ahead) and objects 2–15 m to the right. Across the sequence, the wearer's lower body in Frame 1 and both forearms gripping the club within arm's reach (0.3–0.6 m) in Frames 2 to 5 are segmented at the bottom center, receding toward the lower edge in Frame 5 as the arms drop. In the upper field, the second golfer—who stands 6–8 m ahead facing left with a club in reach and never looks toward the camera wearer—is partially out of view with only legs segmented at the top of Frame 2, fully segmented in Frames 3 and 5, and completely out of frame in Frame 4 as the camera tilts down. While the map highlights tiny distant background figures and objects 8–20 m ahead and 2–5 m to the second golfer's right in Frames 3 and 5 that are hard to spot in the dark RGB background, it omits all scene layout structures and golf equipment—failing to segment the hitting mats, ball tray, basket, yellow dividers, tee ball, and held or spare clubs that are partly occluded or within reach. It is also highly unreliable in class and instance assignments: it fragments the wearer's own left arm, left leg, shoe, and right leg into four separate 'person' instances in Frame 1, mislabels a dark patch at the top left of Frame 2 as a 'car', and misclassifies the distant golf bag stand on the right (8–10 m away) as a 'person' in Frames 3 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in Frame 1 and right hand in Frame 3 (both within 0.4–0.6 m of the camera in the lower foreground) while omitting all yellow body skeletons. By resolving finger and wrist keypoints in Frame 1 (where the left hand reaches down to the left of the extended left leg, about 1 m above the mat) and Frame 3 (where the right hand grips the club shaft above the left hand in front of the torso), the map reveals fine hand orientation and grip articulation during the swing setup that are motion-blurred or small in the RGB strip. However, it provides almost no spatial layout context on its own: it completely misses the camera wearer's legs and torso (0.3–1.2 m away), fails to detect either hand in Frames 2, 4, and 5 as the arms move up and down with the club, and provides no representation of the mat, ball tray (1.5–2.0 m ahead), or spare clubs on the right (1.5–2.0 m). Furthermore, the pose estimator fails to detect the second golfer standing 6–8 m ahead on the forward mat (who faces left away from the range and never looks toward the camera wearer) or the distant figure 15–20 m away in any frame, whether they are partially cropped at the top of Frame 2, fully visible in Frames 3 and 5, or tilted out of view in Frame 4.
